program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s binding and absent criterion are already aligned with the instruction: the edited image shows the book and flowers separated, with no visible overlap or occlusion, and the book appears altered while the requested depth relation is not achieved. Keep unrelated object changes from counting as progress. For robustness, make the binding explicitly resolve “the flower” to the source rose and compare the same book and rose across source and edit; the edit contains two different-looking flowers, so avoid silently treating either as the original reference. Distinguish complete, partial, absent, and unknown by visible evidence of changed depth ordering toward the rose, not mere proximity or object alteration; use unknown only when the image cannot establish that evidence. The five valid, queried traces agree with the reference and show no transport or dependency failure, so there is no basis to weaken the criterion or change the current outcome.
